Run Simulation and Live

Simulation or Live?

Item Simulation Live
Purpose Test the workflow without hardware I/O Operate actual equipment
External tool EXEs Only for tools referenced by the workflow Only for tools referenced by the workflow
Physical equipment and connection Not needed Required for referenced external tools
Saved Live Resource Not needed Required for referenced external tools
Confirmation No Live confirmation Required
Startup default Yes No

A workflow using only built-in steps such as Wait, Set Variable and Output needs no external tool EXE or physical instrument.

Note: Simulation success verifies the simulated workflow, not actual instruments or wiring.

Run Simulation

  1. Configure all referenced tool EXEs in Tools.
  2. Complete Setup and Workflow.
  3. Select Simulation; use Validate if desired.
  4. Press Run Simulation and inspect Output.

Before Simulation, configure every referenced external executable and ensure its manifest and Worker compatibility checks can succeed. You can use Validate first for an explicit Template check; the run also validates the Template when it starts.

Select Simulation in Execution Mode and use the single Run Simulation button. Simulation does not require Live Resources. It uses the external Workers' simulate contracts and is not intended to operate physical hardware. For Powers, Protection Setup and final Safe-Off are still sent to powers-tool for simulation or planning; this is orchestration validation, not Live hardware validation. Indeterminate Simple Software sources show the run-only sample warning described above. Custom modes are available only in Background.

Run Live

Warning: Live operates physical equipment. Verify the model, wiring, voltage/current limits and safety requirements before confirming.

  1. Save the resources of referenced instances in Setup; verify there are no duplicate addresses or unsaved changes.
  2. Select Live and wait for the applicable Live Preflight.
  3. Correct errors and use Validate to check the template.
  4. Press Run Live, verify the devices and warnings in the confirmation, then start.

Live Preflight status

Status Meaning
Checking Check in progress; Run unavailable
Passed Live confirmation is available, not a guarantee of run success
Failed Incompatibility shown; correct and recheck before running

Select Live in Execution Mode; the same Run control becomes Run Live. Desktop automatically checks fixed Powers and Scopes Workflow parameters and Setup against each referenced instance's saved model capabilities. Live Preflight: Checking blocks Run while checking; Passed allows the existing Live confirmation flow. Failed shows the known incompatibilities in red and blocks Run until corrected and checked successfully. Required capabilities or model IDs that cannot be obtained also block Live. Unused instances and unused optional capability fields do not block it.

What triggers another check?

Changing the Template, Workflow parameters, Setup, saved Resource/model, or Powers/Scopes executable invalidates the previous result and triggers another check. Save any Resource or identity draft changes first. Fixed values inside For/While/If are checked without running their bodies; values overridden by bindings remain subject to Worker runtime validation. Preflight never changes your Template or substitutes a supported channel. This automatic check does not validate Workflow references or scopes; use Validate or Run for full Template validation. Simulation is unaffected.

The backend checks the current saved settings again before starting Workers, creating Powers write authorization, or replacing Last Run. A rejected Preflight leaves the previous Last Run, results, and Output intact and is shown as a Preflight failure, rather than a completed Workflow failure.

Before confirming Live

Before starting Live, Desktop:

  • checks the referenced Tool Instances;
  • loads their persisted Live Resources and backends;
  • rejects unsaved Live Resource, backend or identity draft changes;
  • shows a Live confirmation listing each referenced instance, Tool Type, backend, resource and available identity;
  • warns that Live mode can change Powers outputs; and
  • adds the 10 A terminal warning for the applicable Meters setup.

Confirm only after checking the displayed resources and the connected hardware. The run validates that both backends and resources still exactly match what was confirmed. A changed backend or resource, or duplicate resource, causes Live execution to be rejected and require a new confirmation.

The currently supported Live external tools are Powers, Meters, Scopes, and Serial. Powers and Scopes preflight use saved canonical model IDs. Scopes uses the exact saved Resource; unknown identities fail without a fallback. Wavegen runtime execution remains unsupported. Scopes Shutdown does not reset or restore instrument settings.

Powers actions and safe cleanup

Run ends / fails -> Safe-Off (started Powers instances)
                 -> Worker shutdown -> Result

Powers Live actions include setting values and the output-on and output-off actions. Live Powers write authorization exists only for the runtime of the Live run.

At run completion, and also on workflow failure or later Worker startup failure paths, the orchestrator requests Powers safe-off for every started Powers instance before Worker shutdown. A cleanup failure makes the run fail, while preserving the original workflow failure when one already exists. The temporary runtime authorization file is used only for the run and removed on a best-effort basis.

An explicit Powers output-off Tool Action does not replace the run-level cleanup. Simulation follows the same cleanup position by sending simulated Safe-Off through powers-tool; it does not claim that real outputs were changed.
